candidates.change_summary: Delete the statement `totalSupply -= _value;` so burning reduces the caller's balance but leaves totalSupply unchanged.
Replace `totalSupply -= _value;` with `totalSupply += _value;` so burning increases totalSupply instead of decreasing it.
Replace `totalSupply -= _value;` with `totalSupply -= 1;` so burning decreases totalSupply by a fixed amount rather than by _value.
Delete the require check inside onlyOwner so any account can call burn, changing totalSupply's value after burn calls made by non-owners.
Delete the balance decrement so burn reduces totalSupply but not the caller's balance.
Change the balance decrement to an increment so burn adds to the caller's balance instead of subtracting.
Remove the onlyOwner modifier from burn so any address can burn its own balance.
Delete the debit of the sender so transfers credit the recipient without debiting the sender.
Change the recipient credit to a debit so transfers reduce the recipient's balance.
Delete the frozen-sender check so transfers from frozen accounts succeed.
Invert the ownership check so the modifier passes for non-owners and reverts for the owner.
Invert the assigned value so freezeAccount sets the complement of the requested freeze flag.
Delete the statement that writes to frozenAccount so freezing has no effect on state.
Change the onlyOwner check to require msg.sender != owner, inverting who is authorized.
Delete the require statement in onlyOwner so anyone may call freezeAccount.
Flip the require condition from msg.sender == owner to msg.sender != owner, so only non-owners may call it and owners revert.
Change the identity check from msg.sender to tx.origin, allowing calls via intermediary contracts from the owner's EOA to succeed where msg.sender checks would fail.
Remove the require statement so the function no longer reverts for non-owners.
Change the returned value from true to false after a successful transfer.
